dhpak1.3:2.1: “Mind precedes thoughts,” the second verse also [28.159] was recited in the same city,
dhpak1.3:3.1: At Sāvatthī, we are told, lived a Brahmin named Adinnapubbaka.
dhpak1.3:3.2: He never gave anything to anybody, and that is why they called him Adinnapubbaka (Never Gave).
dhpak1.3:3.3: He had an only son who was his darling and delight. Now he desired to have a set of ornaments made for him.
dhpak1.3:3.4: But knowing that in case he gave the commission to a goldsmith, he should have to pay him a fee,
dhpak1.3:3.5: he beat out the gold himself, made him a pair of burnished earrings, and gave them to him.
dhpak1.3:3.6: In this way his son received the name Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī (Burnished Earrings).
dhpak1.3:4.1: When his son was sixteen years old, he had an attack of jaundice.
dhpak1.3:4.2: The mother looked at the boy and said: “Brahmin, your son is sick; have him treated by a physician.”
dhpak1.3:4.3: – “Wife, if I send for a physician, I shall have to pay him a fee in rice; you care nothing about the loss of my substance.”
dhpak1.3:4.4: – “Well, Brahmin, what are you going to do about it?” – “I shall manage things in such a way as not to lose my wealth.”
dhpak1.3:4.5: So he went to various physicians and asked: “What are you in the habit of prescribing for such and such an ailment?”
dhpak1.3:4.6: They mentioned to him bark of trees and this or that.
dhpak1.3:5.1: So he procured these and prepared a remedy for his son.
dhpak1.3:5.2: But in spite of all he did, his son’s condition grew worse and worse, until finally he was past help.
dhpak1.3:5.3: The Brahmin, perceiving that his son was very weak, sent for a physician.
dhpak1.3:5.4: The physician looked at the youth and said: “I have important business to attend to; send for some other physician and have him treat him.”
dhpak1.3:5.5: {1.26} Having thus refused to treat the boy, he turned and left the house.
dhpak1.3:5.6: The Brahmin realized [28.160] that his son was at the point of death.
dhpak1.3:5.7: He thought: “All who come to see this youth will see the wealth in my house; therefore I will place him outside.”
dhpak1.3:5.8: So he carried his son out of the house and laid him down on the terrace.
dhpak1.3:6.1: On that day, very early in the morning, the Fortunate One arose from the attainment of great compassion.
dhpak1.3:6.2: And for the purpose of seeing those who had made their aspiration under previous Buddhas,
dhpak1.3:6.3: those whose roots of merit were fully developed, friends capable of being led,
dhpak1.3:6.4: he surveyed the universe with the Buddha eye, spreading the net of his knowledge over the 10,000 world system.
dhpak1.3:6.5: Straightaway Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī, lying outside on the terrace, appeared within the net of his knowledge.
dhpak1.3:6.6: As soon as the Teacher saw him, he became aware that he had been removed from the house and laid there;
dhpak1.3:6.7: and considering within himself: “Have I sufficient reason for going to him?”
dhpak1.3:7.1: He saw the following: “This youth will repose faith in me, will die,
dhpak1.3:7.2: and will be reborn as a Devaputta in the Realm of the Thirty-Three, in a golden mansion, with a retinue of a thousand Accharās.
dhpak1.3:7.3: The Brahmin will burn his body and will go about the burning-ground weeping.
dhpak1.3:7.4: The Devaputta will survey his own person, three-quarters of a league in height,
dhpak1.3:7.5: adorned with sixty cart-loads of ornaments, surrounded by a thousand Accharās.
dhpak1.3:7.6: And considering within himself: ‘Through what merit have I attained this attainment of splendor?’
dhpak1.3:7.7: he will perceive that he obtained it by reposing faith in me. Then he will say to himself:
dhpak1.3:7.8: ‘My father, who failed to provide medicine for me for fear of wasting his wealth, has now gone to the burning-ground and is weeping.
dhpak1.3:7.9: I will effect a change in his attitude.’ And provoked at his father, he will take the form of Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī,
dhpak1.3:7.10: will go {1.27} to a place not far from the burning-ground, and will fling himself on the ground and weep.
dhpak1.3:8.1: “The Brahmin will ask him: ‘Who are you?’ He will reply: ‘I am your son Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī.’
dhpak1.3:8.2: – ‘Where were you reborn?’ – ‘In the Realm of the Thirty-Three.’
dhpak1.3:8.3: The Brahmin will ask him: ‘What deed of merit did you perform?’
dhpak1.3:8.4: and Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī will tell him that he was reborn in the Realm of the Thirty-Three by reposing faith in me.
dhpak1.3:8.5: Then the Brahmin will ask me: ‘Are there any that have been reborn in heaven by reposing faith in you?’
dhpak1.3:8.6: and I will reply to him: ‘It is not so many hundreds or thousands or hundreds of thousands – there is no counting the number of them.’
dhpak1.3:8.7: I will then recite a verse in the Dhammapada.
dhpak1.3:8.8: At the conclusion of the verse 84,000 [28.161] living beings will obtain comprehension of the Dhamma,
dhpak1.3:8.9: Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī will become a Stream-enterer, and so will Adinnapubbaka the Brahmin.
dhpak1.3:8.10: Thus through this noble youth many will obtain comprehension of the Dhamma.” Of all this the Teacher became aware.
dhpak1.3:9.1: Accordingly, on the following day, having attended to his toilet, he surrounded himself with a large company of bhikkhus,
dhpak1.3:9.2: entered Sāvatthī for alms, and in due course arrived at the house of the Brahmin.
dhpak1.3:9.3: At that moment Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī was lying with face turned towards the house.
dhpak1.3:10.1: The Teacher, observing that he did not see him, sent forth a ray of light. “What is that radiance?”
dhpak1.3:10.2: asked the youth, turning over. Seeing the Teacher from where he lay, he said:
dhpak1.3:10.3: “On account of a foolish father, I have been deprived of the privilege of approaching so excellent a Buddha,
dhpak1.3:10.4: nor have I obtained the privilege either of waiting upon him or of giving him alms or of hearing the Dhamma.
dhpak1.3:10.5: Now I cannot even control the movements of my hands; there is nothing else I can do.”
dhpak1.3:10.6: So saying, he reposed faith in the Buddha. The Teacher said: “He has done enough,” and departed.
dhpak1.3:11.1: A Mind Made Pure As the Realised One receded from his range of vision,
dhpak1.3:11.2: {1.28} Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī died with a believing heart, and as if awaking from sleep,
dhpak1.3:11.3: was reborn in the Deva Realm in a golden mansion thirty leagues in extent.
dhpak1.3:11.4: The Brahmin burned the body of his son, and resorting to the burning-ground, abandoned himself entirely to lamentation.
dhpak1.3:11.5: Every day he would go to the burning-ground and weep and say: “Where are you, my only son?”
dhpak1.3:12.1: The Devaputta, his former son, surveyed his own glory and considered within himself: “By what deed of merit have I obtained this?”
dhpak1.3:12.2: Perceiving that it was by reposing faith in the Teacher, he said to himself:
dhpak1.3:12.3: “This Brahmin failed to provide medicine for me when I was sick, but now goes to the burning-ground and weeps;
dhpak1.3:12.4: I must effect a change in his attitude.”
dhpak1.3:12.5: Accordingly he took the form of Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī, went to a place not far from the burning-ground, and stood wringing his hands and weeping.
dhpak1.3:12.6: The Brahmin saw him and thought to himself: “As for myself, I am weeping because of sorrow for my son; why is yonder youth weeping?’
dhpak1.3:12.7: I will ask him.” So he asked him in the following verse:
dhpak1.3:13.3: holding up your arms, you cry out,
dhpak1.3:13.4: why do you suffer in the woods? [28.162]
dhpak1.3:15.3: but two wheels I cannot find,
dhpak1.3:15.4: through suffering I’ll leave this life. {1.29}
dhpak1.3:16.1: Then said the Brahmin to him:
dhpak1.3:17.1: Whether made of gold, made of jewels,
dhpak1.3:17.2: made of copper, made of silver,
dhpak1.3:17.3: do inform me, O blessed youth,
dhpak1.3:17.4: I will give you the pair of wheels.
dhpak1.3:18.1: Hearing this, the youth thought to himself: “This Brahmin failed to provide medicine for his son.
dhpak1.3:18.2: But seeing that I look like his son, he says: ‘I will procure wheels for your chariot, either of gold or of precious stones or of copper or of silver.’
dhpak1.3:18.3: Very well! I will humble him.” So he said: “How large a pair of wheels will you make for my chariot?”
dhpak1.3:18.4: – “As large as you wish.” – “I want the moon and the sun,” said the youth.
dhpak1.3:18.5: “Give them to me.” By way of request, he said:
dhpak1.3:19.1: The Brahmin youth said this to him:
dhpak1.3:19.2: the sun and the moon are both seen,
dhpak1.3:19.3: my chariot is made of gold,
dhpak1.3:19.4: with a pair of wheels it shines forth.
dhpak1.3:21.1: Youth, wishing for what should not be
dhpak1.3:21.2: wished for, you are surely a fool.
dhpak1.3:21.3: I suppose you will die, but you
dhpak1.3:21.4: will not receive the sun and moon.
dhpak1.3:22.1: But the youth said to him: “But which is the greater fool,
dhpak1.3:22.2: he who weeps for what exists, or he who weeps for what does not exist?” {1.30}
dhpak1.3:23.1: Those who come and go are seen, and colours
dhpak1.3:23.2: are seen on both sides of the street, but he
dhpak1.3:23.3: who made time and passed away is not seen,
dhpak1.3:23.4: which one crying out is the greater fool?
dhpak1.3:24.1: Hearing this, the Brahmin came to the conclusion:
dhpak1.3:24.2: “What this youth says is sensible.” And he said to him.
dhpak1.3:25.1: Youth, you have surely spoken truth,
dhpak1.3:25.2: by crying out I am the greater fool,
dhpak1.3:25.3: like a child who cries for the moon, I wished
dhpak1.3:25.4: for one who is dead and has made his time.
dhpak1.3:26.1: Having thus spoken, freed from sorrow by the words of the youth,
dhpak1.3:26.2: the Brahmin pronounced the following verses in praise of the youth:
dhpak1.3:27.1: I lived like one who was burning, like a fire that was fed by ghee,
dhpak1.3:27.2: like one who was sprinkled with water, all my anguish was extinguished. [28.163]
dhpak1.3:28.1: The dart has been pulled out from me, the grief that was stuck in my heart,
dhpak1.3:28.2: I was one overcome with grief, you dispelled the grief for my son.
dhpak1.3:29.1: The dart has been truly pulled out, I have become calm and cooled down,
dhpak1.3:29.2: I do not grieve, I do not cry, after listening to you, youth. {1.31}
dhpak1.3:30.1: Then the Brahmin asked him: “Who are you?”
dhpak1.3:31.1: Are you a Devatā, a Gandhabba, or are you Sakka, the breaker of towns?
dhpak1.3:31.2: Or whose son are you, and how may I know?
dhpak1.3:32.1: Then answering the question, whose son are you? the youth replied:
dhpak1.3:33.1: I am the one for whom you cry out,
dhpak1.3:33.2: the son burned, lying in the grave,
dhpak1.3:33.3: having done a deed of merit,
dhpak1.3:33.4: I went to fellowship with the Thirty.
dhpak1.3:34.1: A Witness from the Heavens In these words the youth gave him the information he asked for.
dhpak1.3:35.1: I never saw you giving many or
dhpak1.3:35.2: few offerings in your own home,
dhpak1.3:35.4: by what deed went you to the Deva Realm?
dhpak1.3:37.2: with afflicted body in my own home,
dhpak1.3:37.3: the Buddha, free from stain, crossed over doubt,
dhpak1.3:37.4: I beheld, happy, of lofty wisdom.
dhpak1.3:38.1: Confident in mind, and enriched with joy,
dhpak1.3:38.2: I paid respects to the Realised One,
dhpak1.3:38.3: having done this deed of merit,
dhpak1.3:38.4: I went to fellowship with the Thirty. {1.32}
dhpak1.3:39.1: As the youth spoke, the whole body of the Brahmin was suffused with joy.
dhpak1.3:39.2: And this joy he made known in the following verse:
dhpak1.3:40.1: It is wonderful, it is marvellous,
dhpak1.3:40.2: that a deed of respect has such reward,
dhpak1.3:40.3: I am confident in mind, rich with joy,
dhpak1.3:40.4: I go for refuge in Buddha today!
dhpak1.3:42.1: Go for refuge in the Buddha today,
dhpak1.3:42.2: have confidence in Dhamma and Saṅgha,
dhpak1.3:42.3: and in the same way establish the five
dhpak1.3:43.1: Instantly restrain from taking of life,
dhpak1.3:43.2: avoid what’s not been given in this world,
dhpak1.3:43.3: not drinking strong drinks, do not speak falsely,
dhpak1.3:43.4: and be you satisfied with your own wife.
dhpak1.3:44.1: “Very well,” said the Brahmin, agreeing. And he pronounced the following verses: [28.164]
dhpak1.3:45.1: You desire my welfare, Yakkha, desire benefit, Devatā,
dhpak1.3:45.2: I will do as you say, for you are my teacher.
dhpak1.3:46.1: I will go for refuge in the Buddha, and also in the unsurpassed Dhamma,
dhpak1.3:46.2: and in the Saṅgha; to the king of men I will go for refuge.
dhpak1.3:47.1: I instantly restrain from taking life,
dhpak1.3:47.2: I avoid what’s not given in this world,
dhpak1.3:47.3: not drinking strong drinks, I don’t speak falsely,
dhpak1.3:47.4: I will be satisfied with my own wife. {1.33}
dhpak1.3:48.1: Then the Devaputta said to him: “Brahmin, you have much wealth in your house.
dhpak1.3:48.2: Approach the Teacher, give alms, listen to the Dhamma, and ask him questions.”
dhpak1.3:48.3: So saying, he disappeared. The Brahmin went home and said to his wife:
dhpak1.3:48.4: “Wife, I shall invite the ascetic Gotama to my house and ask him questions; therefore prepare hospitality.”
dhpak1.3:48.5: Then he went to the monastery, and without saluting the Teacher or expressing any pleasure at seeing him, stood on one side and said:
dhpak1.3:48.6: “Dear Gotama, consent for today to take a meal in my house with your company of bhikkhus.”
dhpak1.3:48.7: The Teacher consented. As soon as the Brahmin received his consent,
dhpak1.3:48.8: he returned home quickly and caused food, both hard and soft, to be prepared in his house.
dhpak1.3:49.1: The Teacher, accompanied by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus, went to his house and sat down on the seat prepared for him.
dhpak1.3:49.2: The Brahmin waited upon him respectfully. A multitude of people assembled.
dhpak1.3:50.1: We are told that when a man who holds wrong views invites the Realised One, two classes of people assemble.
dhpak1.3:50.2: Those who hold wrong views assemble with the thought in their minds:
dhpak1.3:50.3: “To-day we shall see the ascetic Gotama embarrassed by the questions that are asked him.”
dhpak1.3:50.4: Those who hold orthodox views assemble with the thought: “To-day we shall see the power of a Buddha and the grace of a Buddha.”
dhpak1.3:51.1: Now when the Realised One had finished his meal, the Brahmin approached him,
dhpak1.3:51.2: seated himself on a low seat, and asked him the following question:
dhpak1.3:51.3: “Dear Gotama, are there any that have been reborn in heaven, without giving alms to you, without rendering honor to you,
dhpak1.3:51.4: without hearing the Dhamma, without keeping the Observance Day, solely by making an act of faith?” – “Brahmin, why do you ask me?
dhpak1.3:51.5: Did not your own son Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī tell you that he had been reborn in heaven by reposing faith in me?”
dhpak1.3:51.6: – “When, Dear Gotama?” – “Did you not go to the burning-ground today,
dhpak1.3:51.7: and while you were weeping, see a youth near you wringing his hands and weeping?
dhpak1.3:51.8: {1.34} And did you not say to him: ‘Richly adorned, Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī, bearing garlands, covered with yellow sandal?’”
dhpak1.3:51.9: [28.165] The Teacher related in detail the conversation of the two and told the whole story of Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī.
dhpak1.3:52.1: For this very reason this is called the Buddha’s speech: “Brahmin, it is not a question of one hundred or two hundred –
dhpak1.3:52.2: there is no counting the number of those who have been reborn in heaven by reposing faith in me.”
dhpak1.3:52.3: The multitude were not free from doubt.
dhpak1.3:52.4: The Teacher, perceiving that they were not free from doubt, commanded: “Let the Devaputta Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī come here in his mansion.”
dhpak1.3:52.5: Thereupon Maṭṭhakuṇḍalī drew near, three-quarters of a league in height, his person adorned with celestial adornments.
dhpak1.3:52.6: Descending from his mansion, he worshipped the Teacher and stood respectfully on one side.
dhpak1.3:52.7: The Teacher asked him: “What work of merit did you perform to attain this glory?”
dhpak1.3:53.1: Devatā, with surpassing beauty you stand here,
dhpak1.3:53.2: lighting all directions like the herb-star,
dhpak1.3:53.3: I ask you, Deva of mighty power, what merit did you perform when human?
dhpak1.3:54.1: When the Teacher had completed this verse, the Devaputta replied: “Venerable Sir, I obtained this glory by reposing faith in you.”
dhpak1.3:54.2: – “You obtained it by reposing faith in me?” – “Yes, venerable Sir.”
dhpak1.3:55.1: The populace surveyed the Devaputta and exclaimed: “Marvelous, indeed, are the powers of the Buddhas!
dhpak1.3:55.2: The son of the Brahmin Adinnapubbaka {1.35} obtained glory such as this simply by reposing faith in the Teacher,
dhpak1.3:55.3: without doing a single other work of merit!”
dhpak1.3:55.4: And they were filled with joy. Then the Teacher said to them:
dhpak1.3:55.5: “Our thoughts are the source of all our actions, both good and bad, and by our thoughts are our actions controlled.
dhpak1.3:55.6: For, like a shadow, an act done with thought of faith never leaves a man who goes to the Deva Realm or the world of humans.
dhpak1.3:56.1: Having related this story, the Dhamma king joined the connection, and sealing,
dhpak1.3:56.2: as it were, with the royal seal an edict to which the clay had been attached,
dhpak1.3:57.2: manasā ce pasannena bhāsati vā karoti vā,
dhpak1.3:57.3: tato naṁ sukham-anveti chāyā va anapāyinī.
dhpak1.3:58.1: Mind precedes thoughts, mind is their chief, their quality is made by mind,
dhpak1.3:58.2: if with pure mind one speaks or acts
dhpak1.3:58.3: through that happiness follows one like shadow which does not depart.
dhpak1.3:59.1: At the end of the verse 84,000 living beings comprehended the Dhamma,
dhpak1.3:59.2: and the Devaputta Maṭṭhakuṇḍali was established in Stream-entry, as was the Brahmin Adinnapubbaka.
dhpak1.3:59.3: So far was great wealth confounded in the Buddha’s dispensation.
